2027-02-15.title: Monday of the First Week of Lent
readings: You shall be holy, for I the Lord your God am holy
Your words, Lord, are Spirit and life
Just as you did it to one of the least of these, you did it to me
2027-02-15.alt: Lenten weekday, First Week of Lent. The Alleluia is omitted throughout Lent; the Gloria is omitted except on solemnities and feasts. Liturgical colour: violet.
2027-02-15.verse: And the king will answer them, ‘Truly I tell you, just as you did it to one of the least of these who are members of my family, you did it to me.’
theo: The first full week of Lent opens with the great charter of holiness in Leviticus: “You shall be holy, for I the LORD your God am holy.” We might expect holiness to mean temple rituals, but the commandments that follow are startlingly ordinary. Do not steal; do not lie to one another; do not keep back a labourer's wages until morning; do not curse the deaf or put a stumbling block before the blind; do not slander; do not judge unjustly, favouring either the poor or the great. Then the commandments go down into the heart itself: “You shall not hate in your heart anyone of your kin… You shall not take vengeance or bear a grudge… but you shall love your neighbor as yourself: I am the LORD.” Each command is sealed with the Name of God. Holiness is God's own life, and it shows itself in honest scales, prompt wages, careful words and a heart without grudges.

Jesus draws back the curtain on the last day. The Son of Man sits on his throne of glory, and the nations are gathered before him like a flock at evening. The judgment turns on six simple works: food for the hungry, drink for the thirsty, welcome for the stranger, clothing for the naked, care for the sick, visits to prisoners. Both groups are surprised: “Lord, when was it that we saw you hungry?” And the King answers: “Just as you did it to one of the least of these who are members of my family, you did it to me.” The neighbour of Leviticus has a face, and it is Christ's own. Lent is not first about what we give up but about whom we see. The Church calls these the corporal works of mercy, and on the last day they will be the language in which our love is read.
outline: Ask: if Jesus came to your door today, how would you recognise him?
Point 1 · Be holy as God is holy
Holiness in wages, words and honest dealing.
Point 2 · No grudge in the heart
Point 3 · You did it to me
“Just as you did it to one of the least of these… you did it to me.”
live: Settle any wage, bill or debt you have delayed, today if you can.
Do one of the six works of mercy this week: feed, give drink, welcome, clothe, visit the sick or a prisoner.
2027-02-15.prayer: Holy Father, you call us to be holy as you are holy. Free our hearts from every grudge, make our dealings honest and our words kind, and open our eyes to see your Son in the hungry, the stranger, the sick and the prisoner, so that on the last day we may hear his voice say: Come, you that are blessed. Amen.
altar: At Mass we receive the Body of Christ; on leaving, we meet the same Christ in the least of his brothers and sisters. St John Chrysostom warned that we cannot honour him at the altar and despise him in the poor (in substance).

quick: God says: be holy, for I am holy; do not cheat, lie or hold a grudge.
On the last day Jesus will judge us by our care for the least.
Whatever we do to the poor, we do to Christ.
2027-02-15.action: Do one work of mercy this week for someone who cannot repay you.
2027-02-15.question: In whose face is Jesus waiting for me this Lent?

family.explain: Jesus says: when you give food to a hungry person, or visit someone who is sick, you are doing it for me! Jesus hides in people who need help.
family.intention: We pray for hungry people, sick people and people in prison.
family.ask: Ask: “Who needs our help this week? How can we help Jesus in that person?”

illus: A retired bank clerk in Thrissur began visiting the district jail with a prison ministry group one Lent. He expected to give advice. Instead an old prisoner asked him to sit and listen while he talked about the son who never came. The clerk went home and could not sleep. He said later: I went to visit a prisoner, and the Lord was there before me, waiting to be visited. He has gone every month since.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, King of glory, you hide yourself in the least of your brothers and sisters. Open our eyes to see you and our hands to serve you. Amen.
share: You shall be holy, for I the LORD your God am holy (Leviticus 19:2). Where does holiness need to reach in my daily dealings?
You shall not take vengeance or bear a grudge (Leviticus 19:18). Is there a grudge I carry?
You did it to me (Matthew 25:40). When did I last meet Christ in someone poor?
pm.resp: Lord, make us holy, as you are holy.
interc: For the hungry, the homeless and refugees.
For the sick and those who care for them.
For prisoners and their families, and for prison ministers.
For employers and workers, that wages may be just and paid on time.
For our group, that our Lent may be full of works of mercy.
pm.close: Father, your Son will come in glory to judge the living and the dead. Help us to serve him now in the least, that we may be welcomed into the kingdom prepared for us. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, on this first Monday of Lent God speaks to Moses: you shall be holy, for I the LORD your God am holy (Leviticus 19:2). And then, surprisingly, he talks about wages, lies, slander and grudges.

Holiness is not far away. It is in paying the labourer on time, in not putting a stumbling block before the blind, in refusing to hate in our heart. The commandment ends: you shall love your neighbor as yourself: I am the LORD (Leviticus 19:18).

In the Gospel Jesus shows us the last day. The King will say: I was hungry and you gave me food, I was a stranger and you welcomed me, I was sick and you took care of me, I was in prison and you visited me (Matthew 25:35–36). Both the blessed and the cursed are surprised. Neither saw him.

Lent is a time to open our eyes. Just as you did it to one of the least of these who are members of my family, you did it to me (Matthew 25:40). Let us look for Christ this week in someone poor, sick or forgotten. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says: when you share your food or visit a sick friend, you are doing it for me! This week, do one kind thing for someone who needs help, and remember that Jesus is hiding there.

intro: Theme: “Just as you did it to one of the least of these… you did it to me.”
Holiness in daily dealings, a heart without grudges, and Christ hidden in the least.

points.h: Be holy as God is holy
sub: It shows in wages and words.
Every command sealed with his Name.
q: Speak to all the congregation of the people of Israel and say to them: You shall be holy, for I the LORD your God am holy.
instead, as he who called you is holy, be holy yourselves in all your conduct;
points.apply: Examine your work and business dealings for honesty this week.

sub: Do not hate in your heart.
q: You shall not take vengeance or bear a grudge against any of your people, but you shall love your neighbor as yourself: I am the LORD.
Love does no wrong to a neighbor; therefore, love is the fulfilling of the law.
points.apply: Name one grudge and bring it to confession this Lent.

q: Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the LORD, and will be repaid in full.
And the king will answer them, ‘Truly I tell you, just as you did it to one of the least of these who are members of my family, you did it to me.’
points.apply: Do one corporal work of mercy before Sunday.

concl: Holiness is love made concrete in honest hands and a forgiving heart.
On the last day our love will be read in the language of mercy.
2027-02-15.resolve: Choose one work of mercy to practise every week of Lent.
